text:
jen (Support): Heads up — customer Nimbus opened INC-4532: their Dedicated > Capacity dashboard shows an empty inventory after our control-plane flip during maintenance. Dashboard link: https://console.redwood.com/orgs/nimbus/dedicated/capacity :eyes:

luis (Infra): Thanks Jen. Is this just the UI showing empty rows, or do backend APIs/metrics also look empty? cluster name / org id?

jen (Support): Org ID: org_nimbus_21, cluster: nimbus-prod-west1. UI shows 0 nodes / 0 GPUs. I queried the inventory API and got an empty list:```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.com/internal/v1/dedicated/orgs/org_nimbus_21/pools -> []```Prometheus metrics for node counts still look present (node_up = 42).

ash (SRE): Noted. We flipped the control plane IP and certs rolled at 02:13 UTC. My hunch: telemetry/registration agents didn't re-register with the control plane, so the inventory ingestion stream is stalled. Can someone check telemetry agent status and ingestion queue?

deploy-bot: control-plane-flip completed by ops at 2026-11-09T02:13:08Z :white_check_mark:

luis (Infra): On it. Run this locally or can ops share? Quick check: `kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=telemetry -o wide` — looking for CrashLoopBackOff or restarts. Also check api logs for 401/403 on registration calls.

jen (Support): Running command now, pasting trimmed output:```NAME                                     READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
telemetry-agent-nimbus-0                0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   5          12m
telemetry-agent-nimbus-1                1/1     Running            0          34m
telemetry-agent-nimbus-2                0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   6          12m
```Logs from telemetry-agent-nimbus-0: ```2026-11-09T02:16:10Z ERROR registration failed: POST https://controlplane.cluster.internal/agent/register -> 403 "forbidden: token expired"
stack: agent/register.go:87```

ash (SRE): That aligns — some agents failed to refresh tokens against the rotated control plane. If the inventory ingestion consumer marks those pools as offline while they re-register, the dashboard backend shows empty rows. Two quick mitigations: (1) trigger a resync ingestion for the org (internal API) so the UI pulls historical inventory until agents come back, (2) roll the telemetry-agent DaemonSet with the current control plane cert to force re-registration.

cam (Product): For the customer-facing side: can we make the dashboard show stale data with a warning instead of empty? This is causing alarm. But for now, we need a fast support fix.

luis (Infra): I'm going to trigger the internal resync and then roll the telemetry agents one-by-one. Internal endpoint: `POST https://api.internal.redwood.com/inventory/v1/resync?org=org_nimbus_21` (auth required). Doing it now.

jen (Support): Resync POST returned 202 Accepted. Queue id: q-7f3b. Notified customer that we're working and that this may show as data repopulating shortly.

luis (Infra): Rolling telemetry-agent pods: `kubectl -n redwood rollout restart daemonset/telemetry-agent` — doing a staggered restart to avoid burst. Watching logs...

ash (SRE): After restart, I see agents registering successfully: `INFO registered agent id=telemetry-agent-nimbus-0` and no more 403s. Ingestion consumer lag down from 1h -> 0s.

jen (Support): Update to Nimbus: inventory is reappearing on Dedicated dashboard, GPU rows repopulating. Customer confirmed GPUs visible in UI. INC-4532: resolved with resync + agent rollout.

cam (Product): Follow-up: let's add UI fallback to display last-known inventory with a subtle "data may be stale" banner. Filing a small ticket. :memo:

luis (Infra): Will open infra playbook item to include explicit agent re-registration checks after control plane flips.

jen (Support): Closing the loop here. Thanks all :thumbsup:
